Many pitfalls, the waiter overcharges customers, the experience was not good.
Sep 2026 • Friends
Chinese guests who come to this bar to spend money, please be very careful! We five people pre-booked our seats through the hotel front desk, but when we arrived, they only arranged a table for four on the third floor. I said, the table is too small, we won't be able to fit 6 dishes. The non-gendered service staff in Figure 3 started to trick me. It first arranged us to the very edge of the road where cars were passing by, in a place where we might get rained on. I told it that we have already reserved, and it is not allowed here. It then used translation software to ask me if I was willing to spend 5 million Vietnamese dong to buy the spot inside. There are only 5 of us and only one friend drinking, so we definitely can't spend that much money, so I clearly told it, I'm not willing! So, the female receptionist in Figure 4 used translation software to tell me to wait, and she went to her supervisor to continue communicating to see if they could arrange something for us. After waiting a while, she communicated it well. So they arranged us in a position on the steps where people were coming and going, which was not a good spot, at the edge of the first row in the hall. I naturally assumed they had good communication, and that there wouldn't be any minimum spending requirement here, so we confidently ordered 6 dishes, 3 cans of beer, and 3 cans of coke. We got there after 8 o'clock, ready to pay the bill, when it, whose gender we didn't know, rushed over and said we had to pay 5 million Vietnamese dong. All our actual consumption was only 1.4 million VND, but it told the waiter to quickly get a bottle of 2.5 million VND liquor and another 7 cans of beer to make up the amount. We definitely are not willing. Another manager wearing a floral dress came over to threaten and scare us, saying if we didn't pay, they would call the police. We answer that it's best! But he didn't dare to call the police. After haggling for more than half an hour, we finally backed down and were only willing to spend 2.5 million Vietnamese dong for tonight's expenses. Hua Yi's supervisor initially refused, saying he wanted 3 million. But seeing our firm attitude, they finally had no choice but to compromise. We actually spent 1.4 million VND, plus 18% tax, so they overcharged us by over 800,000 VND. A reminder for Chinese people who want to come here to spend money: if you want to experience a similar lively atmosphere, it's better to go to the other bar not far from the Ho Chi Minh City Opera House. Where is there a place that is as deceptive to customers as a black shop?
